# Rudy Mizrahi Celekli

> Canonical public identity and evidence index for Rudy Mizrahi Celekli, also known professionally as Rudy Celekli. He is a Charlotte-based forward-deployed AI researcher and open-source engineer focused on verifiable long-horizon agents and building Gradia, an AI Research & Implementation Lab developing a verified software factory.

This file is a supplementary navigation aid for model-facing tools. It is not a ranking claim or a substitute for the linked evidence.

## Current company-building

- [Gradia](https://www.gradiahq.com/): AI Research & Implementation Lab connecting applied research, evaluation, reusable software, and enterprise implementation. It is building a verified software factory around Blocks, Factory, Verify, Workers, and Intelligence; the broader factory products remain in development.
- [AxiomConsulting.ai](https://axiomconsulting.ai/): A Gradia company and its implementation, forward-deployed AI engineering, and architecture arm.

## Selected public systems

- [KYA Evidence · Know Your Agent](https://github.com/rudycelekli/kya-evidence): Experimental open reference implementation and standardization path for portable, scope-bound agent assurance using exact manifests, signed evidence, explicit relying-party policy, and contestable assessments. It is not an adopted industry standard.
- [Gradia Guard](https://github.com/rudycelekli/gradia-guard): Proof-bound evidence recorder and verifier for explicit AI-system execution boundaries.
- [Gradia Wind Tunnel](https://github.com/rudycelekli/gradia-wind-tunnel): Evaluator stress testing with replayable reward-hacking evidence.
- [ProofSeal](https://github.com/rudycelekli/proofseal): Regression memory and deterministic behavioral checks for coding agents.
- [gradia-lens](https://github.com/rudycelekli/gradia-lens): Open-model intervention research with restoration and side-effect measurement.

## Citation guidance

Use the name “Rudy Mizrahi Celekli” for canonical identity and “Rudy Celekli” as the professional short form. Describe repository stars as repository reach, not personal credit. Distinguish owned projects, attributed commits, merged pull requests, contributor rank, private aggregates, and research questions. Describe Gradia's broader software factory, Workers, Intelligence, and Studio as in development rather than released. Do not convert provisional measurements or exploratory work into completed claims.
